summary.headline: Gujarat Energy FY26 EBITDA rose to INR3,772 crore (from INR3,241 crore) while PAT was flat at INR2,299 crore; the merger became effective 1 May 2026.
summary.overview: The GSPC/GSPL merger into Gujarat Gas became effective 1 May 2026, with the company renamed Gujarat Energy from 14 May 2026. Q4 FY26 EBITDA was INR943 crore (vs INR790 crore a year earlier), and CNG volume hit a record 3.6 mmscmd. Morbi ceramic demand ramped sharply to about 8 mmscmd after the Middle East conflict constrained propane and LPG supply. Management said FY26 financials are not like-for-like with FY25 because of the demerger and merger accounting, and gave segment EBITDA for the first time on a call. The board recommended a dividend of INR8.90 per share (about INR835 crore outgo).

financial_highlights.change: vs INR790 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR8.90 per share (445% of face value); outgo about INR835 crore

financial_highlights.metric: CGD EBITDA per SCM (FY26, excluding amalgamation impact)

financial_highlights.value: Gas trading about INR400 crore; CGD about INR450 crore; E&P about INR14 crore; renewables about INR5 crore

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Total trading volume was 10.2 mmscmd in FY26, of which about 5.3 mmscmd was intersegment sales to CGD; net external volume was about 4.9 mmscmd, down about 19% from FY25. Management guided trading margins of 4-6% and said FY26 included a one-off of about INR200 crore linked to a Petronet LNG regasification liability, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

segments.name: City Gas Distribution (CGD)
segments.commentary: Q4 CNG volume was a record 3.6 mmscmd (up 12% YoY) across 839 stations, with 17.68 lakh vehicles. Domestic PNG customers crossed 24.18 lakh; Q4 PNG industrial volume was 4.19 mmscmd, up about 7% QoQ. Morbi volume rose 21% QoQ to an average of 2.02 mmscmd in Q4.

segments.name: Exploration and production (E&P)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA was about INR29 crore, but the segment is loss-making after depreciation. Reserves are stated at 6.71 mmboe. FY27 E&P capex is about INR100 crore for planned drilling.

segments.name: Power (renewables / GSEG and GPPC gas-based plants)
segments.commentary: Plant load factors were about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. FY26 segment EBITDA was about INR46 crore (renewables, as stated), and the segment reported losses due to forex and impairment items of about INR15 crore and INR23 crore. The company is reviewing options for the 700 MW combined-cycle plant, whose PPA runs to 2036.

guidance_outlook: CGD margin guidance of about INR5-6 per SCM was given, with a target of about INR5.5-6.5 per SCM; management said trading margins will be maintained.
Morbi price is about INR75 per SCM (non-Morbi about INR68) per management; June was raised by about INR1.5. Management said Morbi demand can reach 8.8-8.9 mmscmd, about 10% above the current level.
FY27 capex guidance: about INR1,000 crore for CGD and about INR100 crore for E&P; no capex for trading.
Gas trading volume is expected to grow 25-30% by FY30-31 from the current 10-12 mmscmd, with prices seen as reasonable from FY28-29.
Tax: about INR1,900 crore of tax losses remain to be used, so no tax is expected on profits up to that amount; the balance is to be used within about 8 years.
GTL demerger share listing is expected to complete by end-July 2026; the listing approval for new Gujarat Energy shares (about 93 crore shares total) is expected within 7-10 days.
capex_capacity: CGD capex guidance is about INR1,000 crore; E&P capex about INR100 crore for drilling a few wells.
Gujarat Energy holds about 36.8-38% of GSPC LNG (investment about INR1,700 crore), following conversion of outstanding amounts into equity; it became a subsidiary.
GSPC Mundra LNG regasification terminal utilisation was about 17% in FY26; it is now at about 35-38% from May 2026.
Management is exploring a dedicated propane import jetty, JT and storage tanks near Morbi, with port authorities in Gujarat under discussion.
Long-term regasification capacity at Dahej is 2.25 MMTPA; long-term LNG totals about 2.96 MTPA (about 10.66 mmscmd).
demand_pricing: Morbi ceramic units on gas rose from 83 (1.66 mmscmd) in March 2026 to 710 units (about 8 mmscmd) by late May 2026; contracts are signed monthly.

Non-Morbi industrial pricing is about INR68 per SCM and Morbi about INR75 per SCM; an analyst's spot-LNG math suggested Morbi margins may be negative at current spot LNG prices, which management did not accept.
Sourcing mix (per management): APM about 2 mmscmd, New Well Gas 0.4-0.5 mmscmd, long-term LNG about 3.5 mmscmd (majority Brent-linked), short-term about 3.5 mmscmd.
FY26 gas trading sales by user: CGD companies about 52-53%, fertilisers about 27%, others (refinery, power, industry) the rest.
Two new long-term LNG SPAs signed in FY26 (Qatar Energy and Uniper, up to 1.36 MTPA combined); Qatar 1 MTPA ramps up to 2030; 2 cargoes already lost in May-June 2026 due to the West Asia conflict.

qa_highlights.question: Is Morbi volume at a peak, and what is the pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Current sales are about 8 mmscmd, with customers indicating up to 8.8-8.9 mmscmd. Pricing is about INR75 per SCM in Morbi and about INR68 elsewhere, indexed to exchange rate and calorific value.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in gas trading and the segment profit baseline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recurring trading run rate is about INR1,000-1,100 crore a year. FY26 included about INR200 crore of one-off liability linked to a Petronet LNG back-to-back arrangement, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the power business and its outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PLF was about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. Management is evaluating reviving the plants through alignment with other businesses. GUVNL pays fixed costs of about INR2.5-3 per unit. Management said the plants are not a drag at present, and a steady-state profit cannot be given until a new arrangement is identified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage LNG price risk as Morbi volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brent-linked long-term volumes from Qatar and Uniper are priced competitively against propane. It is also seeking Henry Hub-linked long-term volumes to give stable pricing for Morbi customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deployment plan for surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has appointed McKinsey to develop a growth and deployment strategy. It expects to share the way forward in the next quarter or a subsequent one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company transfer trading profits to CGD on a cost basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intersegment pricing will be optimised over time as the two segments are evaluated separately. The company now has flexibility to make intersegment sales without the arm's-length constraint.

risks_watch: Propane supply tightness supports Morbi demand, but a normalisation could cut spot prices and volumes; management said it would still compete.
Spot LNG price and INR/USD moves could compress Morbi and CGD margins; an analyst's calculation showed a possible negative spread at spot LNG of about $17-18/MMBtu.

The INR1,334.61 crore trading EBIT includes one-offs, so the recurring run rate may be lower (about INR1,000-1,100 crore per management); also watch intersegment transfer pricing, which shifts profit between trading and CGD.
The power segment (about 1,000 MW) is loss-making with very low PLF; its revival plan and the 700 MW PPA economics are unresolved.

Cash and other financial assets are unclear: management cited about INR5,000 crore cash, while the balance sheet shows about INR1,300 crore cash plus about INR5,500 crore other financial assets, including GSFS-placed funds. The company will provide a breakup.
Watch Q1 FY27 results (early August 2026) for the first post-merger quarter and EBITDA by segment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the merger, the Morbi volume ramp and the long-term sourcing position. Evasive or vague on the power business economics, the cash deployment plan, the transfer-pricing treatment and the balance-sheet cash breakdown, which it deferred to later updates.
key_quotes: We are in the business of making profits, so we cannot be making losses.
The new name reflects the positioning of Gujarat Energy Limited as a true integrated energy Company.
So the price for May was fixed, the price for June is also fixed.
Basically, we have appointed McKinsey. We are working on that.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 CGD EBITDA of INR5.5-6.5/scm and gas trading volume growth of 25-30% by FY30-31; backing is partial, with Morbi demand ramping from 1.66 to about 8 mmscmd (contracts signed monthly, potential 8.8-8.9 mmscmd), CNG volume at a record 3.6 mmscmd, and about INR1,000 crore CGD capex, but no specific new capacity units or timelines were given.
